Name: Autodialer (Automated call campaign) configuration and experience
Description: Need to move this into discovery Epic.  Not part of MVP. Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why): What: In order to reach out to a high volume of members in a cost-effective way, we will employ some form of autodialer, where a member's phone number is automatically dialed by the telephony system, and the call is only routed to a live advocate in the event that a member picks up the phone.  Alternatively, the system might automatically call a member and then play a pre-recorded message if the member picks up, which would also be left as a voicemail if they do not pick up.     Why: The autodialer is essential to keeping costs down, because the percent of members who pick up an a call is likely to be very low, based on similar programs with an outreach component.    Who: The autodialer will be used to outreach to members who are flagged as having a tier 1 or tier 2 medication management trigger.  If the member picks up, the call will be connected to an advocate.   When: The autodialer should trigger calls within the SLA outlined below.  SLAs will be counted starting when the claim is first processed.   Outstanding Questions:Exactly what type of autodialer will we use (e.g. one that leaves a message with a callback option, connects automatically, etc.) Which calls/tiers/triggers will we use an autodialer for.  For example, we may use an autodialer for tier 2 and 3 triggers, but have an agent manually call for tier 1 triggersDo we need to use FIve9 (no autodialer direct to agent capacity available via FIve9)Will we ever autodial anyone but the members, and if so does this effect the build  In Scope:Based on a prioritized list of triggers, we need a mechanism to automatically outreach to members and/or providersAutomated call campaign drivenThis may be outside of Compass based off solution if we chose to send campaign. Name: Prioritize MTM Triggers within all of MTM, and within Subtriggers
Description: Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why): What: Some members may have multiple triggers apply to them at once, from one or more different categories.  For example, a member might be prescribed duplicative medications, be filling a specialty medication for the first time, and also benefit from a program referral.  If a member has multiple triggers that apply to them, we need to prioritize which trigger we act on first.   Why: Some members might not have time to work through all applicable triggers, so we should approach them in order of importance. Additionally, some triggers, like severity 1 drug interactions, might require immediate intervention, and we should bring them up as soon as possible.  When: Once a trigger hierarchy is established, it should be applied to all member data ingested going forward.   Who: The trigger hierarchy will be applied to all members whose health plans pay for Pharmacy Navigator.  Benefit Hypothesis:Establishing a hierarchy with which to outreach to members will be beneficial in several ways:Increase member engagement by surfacing high-impact issues first.Reduce adverse medical events Description: Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why):As a way to Identify which members are the first priority for outreach, I want to build a model that prioritizes any individual member savings opportunity.  I will do this in order to in turn feed into a larger model that prioritizes members for outreach based on their open opportunities.   Benefit Hypothesis:The hypothesis is that we want to create the ost value for our members and have an impact on [NPS], by focusing on opportunities that are more meaningful and impactable.  We will define this in two ways:Meaningful - opportunities for more savings can mean more to the member.  For now we can't do an analysis, but we can eventually analyze how member savings opportunities that are closed correlate with NPS.Impactable - we want to reach out about member savings opportunities that are easier to close, and move a member to being on formulary.  So, cases where a member are off formulary can be prioritized, as well as cases which may require less doctor intervention.  Contacts/Dependencies:This will depend on our use of the member savings data, data which outlines which gaps are easier to close, data which outlines which drugs are in formulary. In Scope:Product to define goal of product by end of day 8/11/25 to know what we should maximize with prioritizationMatt and Adil to connect by EOD 8/11/25 to understand E2E timelines to align DS timelines to his.Below secondary triggers needed to support program with actual rules needed to build - from RTB.Cost effective alternative medication Channel switch Supply switchBe able to prioritize based off overarching Tiers and hierarchy across triggers and other business rules Be able to maintain state of trigger through the life cycleWe need to build a model:Which returns a normalized score that is indicative of which member savings opportunities:Have a larger impact on [NPS or other metric] (cannot analyze this for now, so we can assume this correlates with amount saved)Are higher in proactive resolution rate (ability to close)Move members to on formularyThis needs to be able to run twice per day, and scalable to run for millions of members. Key pieces of data that we will need on each formulary change as of now include:Current drug [ comes from RTB {Savings Advisor}]We need to know the current drug as a baselineCost of current drug, and cost of alternatives [from RTB]We need to know the potential impact to the member if they don't make a change, or the choices available.  Big differences mean high priority.Current days supply and method of receiving drug [from EDP Claims ]Understanding current days supply and means of receiving drug is part of how we would find other drug optionsDuration of current therapy [ from Claim data]A member who has been on a drug for a very long or very short time may impact our decisionTentative: NPS Data [ in EDP]If we have this as a goal - Name: Pulling together trigger scores into a comprehensive member score
Description: Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why):As advocates, they'll need a way to see which members to call first, based on overall prioritization.  Benefit Hypothesis:We hypothesize that by aggregating multiple trigger-level scores—each representing a distinct type of outreach opportunity—into a unified outreach score, we can more effectively prioritize members for engagement. This model will incorporate:Tiered trigger scores (each between 1–100)Reachability score (also between 1–100)The final output will be a composite outreach score (1–100) per member, which reflects both the importance of the opportunity and the likelihood of successful contact.The trigger tiers are defined as:Tier 1 – Clinical Urgency:Opportunities to prevent severe adverse health events (e.g., drug interactions, duplicative therapy)Tier 2 – Member Satisfaction Risk:Events likely to cause dissatisfaction or complaints (e.g., PA denials, formulary changes)Tier 3 – Benefit Optimization:Opportunities to improve member outcomes or reduce costs (e.g., MTM gaps, savings opportunities)By combining trigger-level scores with reachability into a unified outreach score, we expect to:Improve Prioritization AccuracyOutreach will be directed toward members with both high-impact opportunities and high likelihood of engagement.Increase Operational EfficiencyReduces time spent on low-impact or unreachable members.Enhance Member OutcomesEnsures timely intervention for members with urgent or high-value needs.  Contacts/Dependencies:  In Scope:Trigger Score Aggregation:Ingest scores from individual triggers across all three tiers. Each score is normalized between 1–100.Tier Weighting Logic:Apply configurable weights to each tier to reflect business priorities (e.g., Tier 1 > Tier 2 > Tier 3).Reachability Integration:Incorporate reachability score (1–100) to adjust final outreach score.Score Normalization:Final outreach score must be normalized to a 1–100 scale.Output Delivery:Deliver final scores to Compass via HEE for downstream outreach execution.Inputs:Trigger scores (1–100) from Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3Reachability score (1–100)Trigger metadata (e.g., expiration, outreach history)Processing:Apply tier processingCombine weighted trigger scores with reachabilityNormalize final score to 1–100Outputs:Outreach score per memberOutreach disposition flag (first vs re-engagement) - we should check on exactly what is neededEligibility for outreach based on score thresholdFrequency:Model runs at least twice dailyScores refreshed based on latest trigger and reachability data Acceptance CriteriaIDAcceptance CriteriaAC1Model returns a normalized outreach score (1–100) per memberAC2Model ingests trigger scores from all three tiersAC3Model applies tier weighting logic to reflect business prioritiesAC4Model incorporates reachability score into final calculationAC5Model excludes expired or invalid triggersAC6Model distinguishes between first outreach and re-engagementAC7Model scales to over 1 million members and runs at least twice dailyAC8Model output is delivered to Compass via HEEAC9Model supports override logic for clinical severity or business rules  Out of Scope:Individual trigger scoring logic (assumed to be handled upstream)NPS modeling or sentiment predictionResolution guidance or program suppression logicInbound call handling Architectural impacts [links to diagrams, specs, API Contract]:  UX/UI Content [link to wire frames, sketches, designs, project canvas, customer journey, personas]UX/UI Content Engineer:Has Design Review withA11Y elements been completed Accessibility:  Runway items to ensure A11Y compliance and testing are considered  API, Endpoints, URL's:  Provide the impacted components and validate functionality  Use Cases:  Use case descriptions provide a sequence of step an actor has to go through to achieve a goal and also provide details regarding exception alternative flowsPrioritizing members for outreach based on urgency, satisfaction risk, and benefit opportunityAdjusting outreach strategy based on reachabilitySupporting HEE with actionable, ranked member lists Assumptions:   Outstanding Questions: What's the best way to aggregate across tiers?

Name: PharmNav Reporting, Development
Description: As a Product Owner,I want to create a feature for the Pharmacy Navigator that includes a data layer aggregation process, a user-friendly dashboard, and an AI bot agent,So that users can easily access, visualize, and interact with pharmacy data, enhancing decision-making and user experience. Acceptance Criteria:1. Build Data Layer Aggregation Process:Data Integration:Develop a robust data layer that aggregates data from multiple sources (claims data, member engagement metrics, and external databases).Ensure that the data layer supports real-time data updates to provide users with the most current information.Data Quality Checks:Implement validation and cleansing processes to ensure the accuracy and integrity of the aggregated data.Create logs for data processing errors and discrepancies for review.Scalability:Design the data layer to be scalable, accommodating future data sources and increased data volume without performance degradation.2. Build a User-Friendly Dashboard:Dashboard Design:Create an intuitive dashboard that displays key pharmacy metrics, such as Call Acceptance Rate, Authentication Rate, and Engagement Rate, using visualizations like charts and graphs.Allow users to customize their dashboard view by selecting which metrics to display and how to visualize them.Interactivity:Implement interactive features that allow users to filter data by date ranges, pharmacy locations, and other relevant parameters.Enable drill-down capabilities for users to access detailed information from summary metrics.Mobile Compatibility:Ensure that the dashboard is responsive and accessible on various devices, including desktops, tablets, and smartphones.3. Build an AI Bot Agent:AI Bot Development:Develop an AI bot agent that can assist users in navigating the Pharmacy Navigator, answering common queries, and providing insights based on the aggregated data.The bot should be able to understand natural language queries and provide relevant responses or direct users to the appropriate dashboard features.Integration with Dashboard:Integrate the AI bot with the dashboard, allowing users to ask questions about specific metrics and receive real-time data insights.Implement a feedback loop for users to rate the bot's responses, helping to improve its accuracy and effectiveness over time.User Training and Documentation:Provide training materials and documentation for users to understand how to interact with the AI bot and utilize the dashboard effectively.Include FAQs and troubleshooting tips to assist users in resolving common issues.  Benefit Hypothesis: If we implement a data layer aggregation process, a user-friendly dashboard, and an AI bot agent within the Pharmacy Navigator, then users will experience improved access to and understanding of pharmacy-related data, leading to enhanced decision-making, increased user engagement, and ultimately better health outcomes for members. Contacts/Dependencies:  In Scope:  Out of Scope:  Assumptions:   Outstanding Questions:

Name: Real time opportunity close b/w Five9 and Compass
Description: Problem StatementToday, when PN advocate speaks with a member and closes an opportunity in Compass, that closure is not reflected in Five9 in real time. Compass sends the disposition (L1/L2) to HEE  in real time, but Five9 only learns about the closure through scheduled batch files from HEE.Because of this batch-based delay, there are multiple scenarios where Five9 continues to outreach members even after the opportunity has been closed, such as:A member returns a call (inbound) after receiving a voicemail and speaks to an agent before the next batch file is loaded.A member calls in after a warming SMS but before the next file refresh.Opportunity closures that occur between batch windows Due to the non real-time nature of the integration, there will always be gaps where the dialer acts on stale data.Benefit HypothesisIf opportunity closures from Compass are propagated to Five9 in real time, then:Members will not receive duplicate outbound calls after they have already spoken to an agentDialer behavior will more accurately reflect the true state of the opportunityExisting batch files can remain intact while being supplemented by real-time updatesThe window of stale dialing behavior is reduced to near zero (acknowledging rare edge cases)In‑Scope Acceptance CriteriaWhen an agent sets an outcome/disposition in Compass that closes an opportunity:Compass already sends this event to HEE in real timeHEE must immediately notify Five9 to mark the opportunity as non‑dialableFive9 exposes an API that:Accepts Opportunity IDAccepts Dialable FlagNo additional member or opportunity fields are required for this real-time updateOnce an opportunity has been closed via the real-time API:HEE should not resend the same closure via batch files i.e. do not send Duplicate “close” updatesExisting batch files data and cadence can remain as is. The real-time API is additive, not a replacement for batch processing Dependencies:HEEFive9Compass (TBD)- Five9 needs to check if there is a dependency on Compass Out of scope:No new reporting requirements Architectural impacts [links to diagrams, specs, API Contract]:  UX/UI Content [link to wire frames, sketches, designs, project canvas, customer journey, personas]UX/UI Content Engineer:Has Design Review withA11Y elements been completed Accessibility:  Runway items to ensure A11Y compliance and testing are considered  API, Endpoints, URL's:  Provide the impacted components and validate functionality  Use Cases:  Use case descriptions provide a sequence of step an actor has to go through to achieve a goal and also provide details regarding exception alternative flowsUse Case DescriptionPrimary ActorSummaryPre-ConditionsMain Flow (Success Scenario)Alternate FlowException FlowPost ConditionsBusiness Rules Assumptions:   Outstanding Questions:

Name: Enable PA Expiration Opportunities in Compass
Description: Feature DescriptionEnable Compass to display and support a new PA Expiration sub-trigger within the Prior Authorization Support category so Pharmacy Navigator advocates can proactively assist members with renewing an expiring prior authorization before it disrupts access to medication. The opportunity will follow the existing Pharmacy Navigator workflow across Five9 and Compass. When an eligible PA Expiration opportunity is delivered to Compass, the advocate will be provided with the relevant opportunity details, PA-specific talk track, recommended next steps, and standard functionality to document and disposition the interaction.The broader Pharmacy Navigator roadmap supports dedicated Compass views, trigger-specific talk tracks, actionable next steps, and standard opportunity workflows for advocates.Problem StatementPrior authorizations generally require renewal on a defined cadence. When a PA is not proactively renewed by the provider, the member may experience a lapse in medication access or a disruption at the pharmacy. Pharmacy Navigator wants to identify members with PAs approaching expiration and enable advocates to proactively help coordinate the renewal process, with the member’s permission, before the PA expires.Benefit HypothesisIf Pharmacy Navigator advocates can see PA Expiration opportunities in Compass and receive the appropriate member context, talk track, and next steps, they can proactively help members initiate the renewal process and reduce the risk of medication disruption at the pharmacy.This capability is intended to:Improve the member experience by addressing potential PA issues before expiration.Provide advocates with clear and consistent guidance for PA renewal outreach.Reduce unnecessary outreach when the PA has already been renewed or renewal activity has begun.Allow PA Expiration opportunities and outcomes to be distinguished from other Prior Authorization Support opportunities.The Pharmacy Navigator reporting architecture currently incorporates Compass cases, support tasks, opportunity dispositions, Five9 calls, and trigger or campaign mappings, which supports the need to identify the new sub-trigger consistently across systems. User StoryAs a Pharmacy Navigator advocate,I want to see a PA Expiration opportunity in Compass with the member’s relevant PA information, expiration timing, talk track, and recommended next steps,so that I can proactively help the member begin the PA renewal process and reduce the risk of a disruption in medication access.In Scope1. New Opportunity Sub-TriggerAdd PA Expiration as a new sub-trigger under the Prior Authorization Support category.Display the sub-trigger consistently within:The active Pharmacy Navigator opportunity.Opportunity details.Opportunity history.Available outcome or disposition workflows, where applicable.Follow the existing Compass workflow used for other Pharmacy Navigator opportunities.The previously documented solution direction also calls for PA Expiration to appear in Compass with the correct sub-trigger, expiration timing, work instructions, and talk track.  Also add to Pharmacy Navigator Sub Category. 2. Opportunity InformationWhen Compass receives a PA Expiration opportunity, display the available information needed by the advocate to understand and act on the opportunity, including:Opportunity ID.Opportunity category: Prior Authorization Support.Opportunity sub-trigger: PA Expiration.PA expiration date or expiration timing.Relevant medication or drug information.PA identifier, if provided downstream.Recommended next step or work instruction.Current opportunity status.Available opportunity history.Final required data elements will depend on what is included in the downstream payload. Internal solution discussions identified member identifier, PA identifier, drug information, expiration date, eligibility information, and event timestamp as potential event elements, but the finalized Compass payload is not specified in the available source. 3. Advocate Talk TrackDisplay the PA Expiration talk track provided and approved by Pharmacy Navigator Business Product.The talk track should help the advocate:Explain that the member’s PA is approaching expiration.Confirm whether renewal activity has already begun.Obtain the member’s permission before providing renewal assistance.Explain the available Pharmacy Navigator support.Document the result of the conversation.Talk track content must be configurable or updated through the existing Compass content process, where supported.4. Advocate WorkflowThe advocate must be able to:Open and review the PA Expiration opportunity.View the PA expiration context and talk track.Record whether the member was reached.Document the interaction outcome using the existing Pharmacy Navigator workflow.Create or complete any applicable follow-up or support task using existing Compass functionality.Update or close the opportunity through the standard workflow.View the opportunity and documented outcome in history.Existing roadmap materials identify opportunity history, support-task workflows, opportunity outcomes, and Compass advocate views as part of the Pharmacy Navigator operating model. 5. Opportunity Suppression and ClosureUpstream systems must prevent or stop outbound activity when:The PA has already been renewed.A new PA or renewal process has already been initiated.The medication is included on the Medical Affairs exclusion list.The member does not have an eligible phone number.The member does not have the required outreach permission.Another applicable outreach suppression rule is present.If renewal activity begins after the opportunity has been sent downstream, but before outreach occurs:Additional outbound outreach must be stopped.Compass must receive the applicable opportunity status update or closure instruction.The opportunity must no longer appear as actionable for outbound outreach.The status change should remain visible in opportunity history, if supported by the existing workflow.The existing roadmap includes real-time closure between Five9 and Compass as a planned mechanism for preventing duplicate outreach on closed opportunities. Existing Pharmacy Navigator discussions also reference a Compass, Five9, and HEE disposition mapping artifact that should be used to confirm the final status synchronization approach. 8/27 update: Five9 work will be captured in a separate feature. Amit is checking to see if we even need Five9 involvement for this effort.6. Reporting and TraceabilityCompass must make the PA Expiration sub-trigger and associated outcomes available through existing downstream reporting feeds so reporting can distinguish these opportunities from other Prior Authorization Support opportunities.Where supported by the existing model, reporting should be able to identify:PA Expiration opportunities delivered to Compass.Opportunity statuses.Advocate interaction outcomes.Opportunity or support-task dispositions.Closed or suppressed opportunities.Outreach completion status.Internal solution discussions specifically identified Compass and reporting as systems requiring updates for the new trigger.Acceptance CriteriaAC1: Display the PA Expiration Sub-TriggerGiven Compass receives a valid Pharmacy Navigator opportunity categorized as Prior Authorization Support with a PA Expiration sub-trigger,When the advocate opens the opportunity,Then Compass displays:Category: Prior Authorization SupportSub-trigger: PA ExpirationThe opportunity using the existing Pharmacy Navigator opportunity workflow.AC2: Display PA Expiration InformationGiven the PA Expiration opportunity payload includes PA and medication information,When the advocate views the opportunity details,Then Compass displays the available:PA expiration date or timing.Medication or drug information.PA identifier.Opportunity ID.Opportunity status.Recommended next steps.And Compass does not populate missing values with inaccurate or inferred information.AC3: Display the Approved Talk TrackGiven a PA Expiration opportunity is opened,When the advocate views the opportunity,Then Compass displays the approved PA Expiration talk track provided by Pharmacy Navigator Business Product.AC4: Support Existing Advocate WorkflowGiven the advocate is working a PA Expiration opportunity,When the advocate completes the member interaction,Then the advocate can:Document the interaction.Select an applicable outcome or disposition.Complete applicable follow-up actions through the existing workflow.Update or close the opportunity.View the documented activity in opportunity history.AC5: Do Not Create Outreach Based on Missing EligibilityGiven a member does not have an eligible phone number or the required outreach permission,When upstream eligibility and outreach rules are evaluated,Then the opportunity is not routed for outbound outreach.And Compass is not responsible for independently calculating phone or permission eligibility unless separately defined during solutioning.The requirements shared in earlier internal discussions also specify that only members with a phone number and appropriate permissions should receive outreach. AC6: Suppress Already Renewed PAsGiven the upstream source indicates that the PA has already been renewed,When opportunity eligibility is evaluated,Then the PA Expiration opportunity is not routed for outreach.AC7: Suppress Renewal Already in ProgressGiven the upstream source indicates that a new PA or renewal process has already begun,When opportunity eligibility is evaluated,Then the PA Expiration opportunity is not routed for outreach.AC8: Exclude Identified MedicationsGiven the medication is included on the Medical Affairs exclusion list,When opportunity eligibility is evaluated,Then the PA Expiration opportunity is excluded from outreach.And the exclusion list is managed upstream and is not maintained through this Compass feature unless separately agreed.AC9: Stop Outreach Following New PA ActivityGiven a PA Expiration opportunity has been delivered downstream,And outreach has not yet occurred,When Compass receives an update indicating that renewal activity has started,Then the opportunity is no longer presented as actionable for outbound outreach.And the applicable updated or closed status is reflected in Compass.And the status change is retained in opportunity history where supported by the standard workflow.AC10: Preserve Completed OutreachGiven outreach has already occurred,When new PA activity is received afterward,Then Compass retains the completed advocate interaction and outcome history.And no additional outreach is initiated for the same PA Expiration opportunity.AC11: Support Existing Dispositions and ReportingGiven the advocate documents an outcome for a PA Expiration opportunity,When the interaction is saved,Then Compass passes the sub-trigger, status, and applicable disposition through the existing downstream integration and reporting workflow.AC12: Maintain PA Expiration TraceabilityGiven a PA existing Pharmacy Navigator history experience.

Name: Integrate Pharmacy Navigator within CMK Chat (Digital CMK Chat Team)
Description: Problem StatementToday, Pharmacy Navigator (PN) primarily engages members through outbound and inbound phone interactions. While this white-glove advocacy model delivers strong outcomes, many members are unable or unwilling to engage via phone during working hours, creating a barrier to reach and engagement. At the same time, Caremark members are increasingly engaging through digital channels. Industry competitors such as Rightway have adopted chat-first advocacy models, with market intelligence indicating that the majority of member interactions occur through digital messaging experiences. Additionally, Pharmacy Navigator's roadmap and discovery efforts have identified chat as a strategic capability to improve reach, advocate efficiency, and integration within the Caremark digital ecosystem.  Currently, there is no direct pathway for Pharmacy Navigator-eligible members using Caremark Chat to connect with specialized PN advocates who have the context, tools, and expertise required to resolve pharmacy-related barriers.Feature OverviewEnable Pharmacy Navigator as a specialized support destination within the existing Caremark Chat experience. When a Pharmacy Navigator-eligible member requests live assistance within Caremark Chat, they will be seamlessly routed to a dedicated Pharmacy Navigator advocate during PN Hours of Operation. The advocate will receive relevant member context and continue delivering the same high-touch advocacy experience currently available through phone interactions.This approach leverages existing Caremark chat capabilities while extending Pharmacy Navigator support into a member-preferred digital channel.Hypothesis StatementIntroducing Chat as a Pharmacy Navigator engagement channel will improve member access to PN services by providing a convenient, asynchronous alternative to phone outreach while maintaining the same high-touch advocacy experience.Business Outcome HypothesisBy enabling PN members to connect with specialized advocates through chat, we expect to:Increase member reach and engagement rates.Provide an alternative engagement path for members unable to answer phone calls.Improve advocate productivity through concurrent chat handling.Strengthen integration between Pharmacy Navigator and Caremark digital experiences.Increase Pharmacy Navigator utilization and visibility.Position Pharmacy Navigator competitively alongside emerging navigation and advocacy solutions. Why This MattersPharmacy Navigator was designed to provide proactive, white-glove pharmacy advocacy and support. Its success depends heavily on member engagement. Today, phone remains the primary engagement channel, but internal discovery identified chat as a key opportunity to improve reach by giving members another way to access support. Estimates from roadmap discussions projected chat could increase reach through an additional engagement channel while simultaneously expanding advocate capacity.  By embedding Pharmacy Navigator into Caremark's digital ecosystem, members can receive support at the moment they encounter friction, rather than waiting for an outbound call or navigating multiple support channels. What Does the Data Say?Caremark.com Chat31.7% of members who contacted Caremark (call or chat) have a registered Caremark.com account.2.7% of members who logged into Caremark.com clicked the Chat icon. Chat Volumes Across PN Pilot ClientsClientChat InteractionsWBD334 (1.11%)St. Jude222 (1.71%)Workday203 (0.88%)Halliburton204 (0.57%)THR308 (0.64%)These volumes indicate an existing member appetite for chat-based support and provide a baseline for pilot planning. In Scope (Phase 1 Pilot)Member ExperienceLeverage the existing Caremark Chat experience:AI Chat → Live Agent Chat → Phone Support (Optional)RoutingIdentify PN-eligible members during the chat experience.Route eligible members requesting a live agent to specialized PN advocates during PN Hours of Operation.Outside PN Hours of Operation, route members through the standard Caremark support workflow.Allow advocates to share the PN toll-free number when a member prefers phone support.Experience GoalsNo additional steps for the member.Seamless transition from general digital support to specialized pharmacy advocacy.Maintain PN's white-glove experience regardless of channel.Advocate ExperienceProvide advocates with sufficient context to continue servicing members effectively without requiring channel switching.Member Context Available at Chat StartClient NameOpportunity TypeTrigger ReasonOutreach HistoryPrevious CallsPrevious ChatsPrior Authorization StatusFormulary InformationOpen Support TasksResearch has shown advocates are most effective when they can immediately see the member's pharmacy journey and support history. Similar requirements were identified during PN chat discovery efforts. Pilot ObjectivesEstablish PN chat workflows.Validate advocate adoption.Validate member adoption.Capture operational learnings.Gather advocate feedback to prioritize future enhancements.Success MetricsMember EngagementChat VolumeUnique Members Engaged via ChatChat Engagement RateReach Rate Impact (Chat vs. Phone Only)Advocacy OutcomesChat-to-Case Conversion RateResolution RateMember Satisfaction (CSAT)Average Time to ResolutionOperational MetricsAdvocate UtilizationConcurrent Chat CapacityAverage Chat Handle TimePercentage of PN-Eligible Members Successfully RoutedBusiness MetricsIncremental ReachIncremental EngagementPharmacy Navigator Utilization GrowthReduction in General Care Center Transfers
